# Concurrent cold native unwind diagnostic

This fork-only GitHub Actions workflow validates a public AnyPS5 native guest relinking and user-space PRX/libkernel cancellation boundary. It does not modify the host kernel or produce production `ci.json`/Full-suite evidence.

The frozen original baseline is `9aa5fd290007d816bfed6970ee259f9baaa0e24e`, the historical unbounded-waiter comparison is `b758d156dd850da84e166b14f282cbba393d331c`, the earlier fail-closed candidate is `0186b61026aefd76124ef30b9b07de8a43b3bb05`, and the candidate is `ce5c0c571f5c72de6d21269f6e18c683211ed64e`. The baseline runs the cold single-worker and two-worker EventFlag cancellation boundaries plus three exception controls. Its two cancellation cases are expected to preserve the original SIGSEGV fault. The 0186 lane overlays the exact same fixture and registration, proves both non-mutating wait observations and the resolver gate were reached, then preserves the real contender cancellation failure. The legacy lane runs the direct resolver contention test and must fail the named pre-release-return assertion. The candidate runs six essential cases: cold cancellation, direct resolver contention, concurrent cold cancellation, and the three exception controls.

The candidate concurrency case starts two real pthread workers on separate single-waiter guest EventFlags (`EVF_ATTR_SINGLE`, `0x10`). After releasing each worker to its wait, the test repeatedly calls `sceKernelPollEventFlag` on each flag until it returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EPERM` (`0x80020001`), which the pinned EventFlag implementation returns when `_waiters != 0` for a single-waiter flag. Before that state, only `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EBUSY` (`0x80020010`) is accepted. This poll holds the EventFlag mutex only for the API call and does not change the pattern or cancellation generation or notify waiters. A test-only gate pauses the first resolver after global state changes to resolving but before native symbol lookup. The second worker is then cancelled through the actual libkernel wait/personality/cleanup/Resume path. It must join as `PTHREAD_CANCELED` while the winner is still held; only then is the winner released and joined. Trace assertions check native personality and Resume addresses/owners, exact exception-marker association, matching target source, both caller-frame cleanup counts, both pthread cleanup handlers, and that the contender used one local validated pair through matching Resume. The test-only instrumentation is null-default and compiled only for Linux tests.

The base fixture has no resolver test observer, so the same real two-worker boundary uses two single-waiter EventFlags and non-mutating poll observations without the test gate; it must retain the original SIGSEGV red. It does not claim to exercise local-pair contention on the base. The legacy lane gets only the public fixture, CMake test registration, and the existing test-only gate/count patch; it retains the old resolver implementation and must fail `loserReturnedBeforeRelease`. Candidate-only target-pair instrumentation is stripped from the base/legacy CMake overlays so those trees do not compile or call APIs they do not contain.

CTest output limits are checked and set to 1 MiB; the workflow retains raw `LastTest.log`, XML, `--output-log`, build/configure logs, identities, and patches. Candidate trace records are labeled by worker and checked for complete contiguous event indices and the expected local/published pair source. All cases are exact-counted and skip-free. The workflow retains actor and triggering-actor authorization checks, the fork-parent check, schema-only historical input `3391`, read-only workflow permissions, and a finite job timeout.

No workflow dispatch, remote push, Full validation, topic-branch publication, PR, title probe, GPU claim, or gameplay claim is authorized by this driver revision until a separate coordinator release.
